data.exact_reserve_text: In 2017, there has been an overall net surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 2.9m (2016: GBP 20.1m) due to lower than expected incurred movements across most classes of business. This was primarily due to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2014 and prior accounts following improvements in State Volunteer and NECC contracts during 2017. The 2016 year of account deterioration during 2017 is due to fall back exposure to the hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria.

data.standardized_narrative: At the 2017 year-end the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding (prior-year balance) was GBP 350.266m. During 2017 there was an overall net favourable development (release) in ultimate claims of GBP 2.9m driven principally by lower-than-expected incurred movements across classes - notably a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on 2014 and earlier years - partially offset by deterioration due to fall-back exposure to the 2017 hurricanes (Harvey, Irma and Maria) which affected the 2016 year of account.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from the Statement of Financial Position liabilities (Claims outstanding, 2016 comparative column). No explicit GROSS prior-year movement (PYD) labelled 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' was found; the report explicitly states an overall NET surplus (release) in ultimate claims of GBP 2.9m and that net figure has been used as the PYD fallback (NET of reinsurance). RITC and accepted reinsurance (Syndicate 6103) and foreign-exchange movements may distort year-to-year comparisons. Claims development triangle is present (gross), and has been included in _claims_triangle. Amounts in the triangle are presented in the report in GBP '000 (thousands).
